title.en: From the post box to the satellite

text.en: A letter once took days to cross the country, and a message now takes less than a second. In the same way, trade has moved from exchanging goods for goods to a worldwide market. This lesson covers how India communicates, and how it buys and sells.

Communication is the exchange of information, thoughts and ideas, and it is classified into personal communication and mass communication.
Personal communication is the exchange of information between individuals and includes the post, telephone, mobile, SMS, fax and the internet.
The Indian postal network is the largest in the world with about 1,55,000 post offices, of which more than 1,39,000 are in villages.
The postal service opened to the public in 1837, the first postage stamp was issued in 1852 at Karachi, and the PIN code system was introduced in 1972.
The Quick Mail Service started in 1975, and premium services include Speed Post, money order, e-money order, Business Post and Express Parcel Post.
India has one of the largest telecommunication networks in Asia, and more than two-thirds of villages have STD facilities, while ISD is used for international calls.
Mass communication gives information to millions of people at the same time, educates, entertains, and creates awareness about national policies.
Mass communication works through print media, which means newspapers, and electronic media, which means radio, television, the internet and social media.
Radio broadcasting began in 1923 with the Radio Club of Bombay, it became All India Radio in 1936 and was renamed Akashvani in 1957.
Television in India is called Doordarshan, which reaches backward and remote rural areas through the Common National Programme.
The internet is a global system of interconnected computer networks, and social media are interactive technologies for creating and sharing information and ideas.
Satellite communication gives a continuous view of large areas, and it is used for weather forecasting, tracking natural disasters and border surveillance.
The Indian Space Research Organisation was established in 1969, and since then satellites have opened a new era in communication.
India's satellite systems are INSAT, the Indian National Satellite System, and IRS, the Indian Remote Sensing Satellite System.
INSAT was established in 1983 as a multipurpose system for telecom and weather, and INSAT-1B launched on 30 August 1983 was the first of the series.
Other communication satellites are GSAT, Kalpana-1, HAMSAT and EDUSAT, and GSAT-7A was launched on 19 December 2018.
Trade is the act of buying, selling or exchanging goods and services, and it decides the economic growth of a country.
The oldest method of trade was barter, in which goods were exchanged for goods, and later money became the medium of exchange.
Balance of trade is the difference between the value of imports and exports, favourable when exports exceed imports and unfavourable when imports exceed exports.
Internal trade is carried on within the country, also called domestic or local trade, uses local currency and mainly roads and railways, and it helps balanced regional growth.
International trade, also called external or foreign trade, is between two or more countries, uses foreign currency and mainly waterways and airways.
Export means goods and services sold abroad for foreign currency, and import means goods and services bought from overseas producers.
Trade between two countries is bilateral trade, and trade among more than two countries is multilateral trade.
India's major exports include tea, coffee, marine products, ores and minerals, leather goods, gems and jewellery, sports goods, chemicals, textiles, engineering and electronic goods.
India's major imports are petroleum products, pearls and precious stones, gold and telecom instruments, with petroleum the biggest import.

problem.en: India's exports in a year are worth 300 units and imports 450 units. Find the balance of trade and say whether it is favourable.

text.en: Balance of trade = value of exports minus value of imports.

why.en: This is the definition from the textbook.

text.en: 300 minus 450 gives minus 150, so imports exceed exports by 150 units.

why.en: A negative figure means a deficit.

text.en: Since imports are more than exports, the balance of trade is unfavourable.

prompt.en: Explain to a friend the difference between personal and mass communication, and between internal and international trade, with one example each.

requiredIdeas.en: Personal communication is between individuals, for example the postal service or mobile phone
Mass communication reaches millions at once, for example television or newspapers
Internal trade is within the country using local currency, while international trade is between countries using foreign currency

commonMisconceptions.en: INSAT is a remote sensing satellite system (INSAT is for communication and IRS is for remote sensing)
A favourable balance of trade means imports exceed exports (it means exports exceed imports)

points.en: Communication is personal (post, phone, internet) or mass (print and electronic media).
ISRO was set up in 1969, INSAT in 1983, and satellites help weather and disaster monitoring.
Trade is internal or international, with export and import as its components.
Balance of trade is exports minus imports, and petroleum is India's biggest import.
